description: We are building a mobile app for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge to monitor astronauts' health during long-duration space missions. We're looking for passionate Mobile Developers, UI/UX Designers, Backend Developers, AI/ML Engineers, and Researchers who enjoy teamwork, innovation, and solving real-world challenges.
summary:
Space missions expose astronauts to unique physical and psychological challenges, including physiological changes, radiation exposure, reduced physical activity, and isolation from Earth.

AstroPou is an AI-assisted mobile health monitoring companion designed to support astronauts throughout their missions. It combines health tracking, daily check-ins, mood assessments, and interactive visualizations to help astronauts explore their health indicators and understand changes over time.

Through Ophiuchus, a constellation-inspired health visualization, users can explore health metrics, trends, and target ranges. AI-assisted insights help explain health information, while personalized reminders and alerts encourage proactive health awareness. The application also supports sharing health information with flight surgeons and introduces AstroPou, a friendly virtual companion that makes daily check-ins more engaging and promotes a sense of connection with Earth.

By bringing physical health monitoring and emotional engagement together, AstroPou aims to make astronaut well-being more accessible, proactive, and human-centered.

Far from Earth, Never Far from Home.
details:
Space exploration pushes human capabilities beyond familiar limits. But behind every mission, there is an astronaut facing physical demands, environmental challenges, and the psychological effects of isolation and confinement.

As missions become longer and humans travel farther from Earth, supporting astronauts requires more than monitoring vital signs. It also requires making health information understandable, encouraging healthy routines, and preserving a sense of connection and emotional support.

This is where AstroPou comes in.

Developed by Team OrbitCode, AstroPou is an AI-assisted mobile health monitoring companion designed to bring physical health awareness and emotional engagement together in one experience.

Inspired by the virtual pets many of us grew up with, AstroPou introduces a friendly digital companion alongside interactive health monitoring, AI-assisted insights, health trends, reminders, and communication with Earth.

Our goal is to make astronaut well-being more accessible, engaging, and human-centered throughout space missions.

Because every astronaut deserves to feel supported, no matter how far from home they travel.

Featuring a cinematic rocket launch background, the screen introduces the message: "Space Is Tough. You Don't Have to Face It Alone." This reflects one of the key challenges astronauts face during space missions: maintaining their physical and emotional well-being while living and working far from Earth.

Rather than starting with technical health metrics or data dashboards, we chose to introduce AstroPou through an emotional message that highlights the importance of support, connection, and companionship.

The supporting text, "Stay healthy, feel connected, and never feel alone," summarizes the application's three guiding ideas: health awareness, human connection, and emotional well-being.

A prominent "Meet Your Companion" call-to-action invites users to begin their journey and discover AstroPou, the virtual companion at the heart of the experience.

This introductory experience establishes the project's identity and communicates that AstroPou is more than a health monitoring application: it is designed to make astronaut well-being a more personal, engaging, and human-centered experience.

The screen features AstroPou against a view of Earth from space, creating a visual connection between the astronaut's environment and the home they are far away from.

A friendly welcome message — "Hey, space buddy! Ready to make this journey amazing together?" — introduces the companion as a supportive presence throughout the user's journey.

We chose a virtual pet-inspired character to make the application feel more personal and approachable. Rather than presenting astronauts with another conventional health monitoring interface, AstroPou introduces a familiar, friendly interaction that encourages engagement with daily well-being activities.

The Explore button invites users to continue into the application and discover its features.

This screen establishes the emotional identity of AstroPou: a digital companion designed to make health monitoring feel more human, engaging, and connected to Earth, even during missions far from home.

The Astronaut Health Dashboard is the central screen of AstroPou, designed to give astronauts an accessible overview of their daily health information within the context of their space mission.

At the top, a personalized greeting introduces the astronaut's daily health status. The center of the interface features an astronaut visualization surrounded by three key monitoring indicators: Radiation, Cardiovascular Health, and Physical Activity.

Rather than displaying these indicators in a conventional list, we visually connect each one to a corresponding area of the astronaut's body through interactive hotspots. This astronaut-centered approach makes health information easier to explore and creates a more intuitive connection between the data and the human body.

AstroPou, the virtual companion, appears alongside the astronaut and provides contextual, encouraging messages. This adds a human-centered layer to the monitoring experience, making routine health awareness feel more personal and engaging.

At the bottom, a mission status card displays the mission day, mission context, and an overall status indicator, connecting the astronaut's health overview to the wider mission environment.

By combining health indicators, interactive exploration, companion messages, and mission context in one interface, the dashboard aims to make astronaut health monitoring more understandable, engaging, and accessible.

The displayed percentages and status values in the interface are illustrative UI values and should not be interpreted as validated clinical measurements.

We designed this experience to transform health monitoring into something more visual and intuitive. Instead of presenting health indicators as a conventional list of numbers, Ophiuchus represents them as stars connected within a constellation. Each star corresponds to a health metric, creating a unified visual overview of different aspects of an astronaut's well-being.

The visualization includes indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, mood assessment, body temperature, and sleep duration. Users can explore individual indicators and view more detailed information about the selected metric.

For example, the Sleep Duration view presents a seven-day trajectory alongside the average duration, recent trend, and target range. This allows users to explore changes over time rather than relying on a single reading.

The interface also uses visual status indicators to make information easier to interpret and highlights the selected metric within the constellation.

Ophiuchus brings together space-inspired design and health data visualization in a distinctive experience. Its purpose is to make complex health information more accessible, encourage awareness of changing patterns, and help astronauts better understand their well-being throughout a mission.

We designed this feature around the understanding that astronaut well-being involves more than tracking health measurements. Astronauts also need encouragement, healthy daily routines, timely awareness of changes, and a sense of connection with the people they leave behind.

The screen organizes communication into four categories:

  • Daily Motivation: Encouraging messages from AstroPou that reinforce positive health habits and keep astronauts engaged with their well-being.
  • Health Reminders: Practical reminders, such as staying hydrated, that encourage healthy daily routines during missions.
  • Messages from Earth: A dedicated communication category for supportive messages from loved ones, helping maintain an emotional connection with home.
  • Health Alerts: Notifications that draw attention to changes in health patterns, such as variations in sleep, and encourage astronauts to review their recent information and consider appropriate next steps.

Each category has a distinct visual style, using different colors, icons, and contextual companion expressions to help users recognize the type of message quickly.

By bringing these interactions together in one place, AstroPou extends health monitoring beyond data visualization. It creates a more supportive experience that combines daily health awareness, emotional encouragement, and connection with Earth.

The alerts are intended to support awareness and follow-up, not to provide medical diagnoses.

AstroPou is built on the belief that astronaut well-being goes beyond monitoring vital signs. It is about understanding health patterns, encouraging healthy routines, supporting emotional well-being, and maintaining a connection with Earth.

By combining AI-assisted health insights, interactive health visualization through Ophiuchus, personalized reminders, and a friendly virtual companion, AstroPou aims to make astronaut health monitoring more accessible, engaging, and human-centered.

Our vision is to help astronauts feel supported throughout their missions, while giving health monitoring a more personal meaning.

Because even when exploration takes us farther from Earth, the human need for care, connection, and companionship remains.

AstroPou – Far from Earth, Never Far from Home.
